accepted.A4: Closed under the stop rule agreed after five review rounds. (1) Telling a 100 ms debounce from 150 ms needs a fake clock; the 190 ms sample rules out searching with no debounce. (2) No results on an empty query or on first load is a follow-up. (3) Keyboard moves over a list with date and document options are a follow-up. (4) Dates count calendar days from TODAY, as the reference does; millisecond arithmetic fails only where a DST change falls between 12 March and 1 April, so the zone the checks run in decides whether it is caught.
accepted.A5: Keyboard rules run on one list of four commands; a mixed list with date and document options, of another length, is a follow-up.
accepted.B4: (a) A failed search has not answered with results, so everything has not answered and No results stays hidden; a clearer sentence is a follow-up. (b) in 5 day and in 1 days are neither stated nor checked. A command click and No results on an empty query are follow-ups.
accepted.C2: The 190 ms sample proves the search did not answer without a debounce. Telling 100 ms from 150 ms, or showing that a second key inside the window drops the first search, needs a fake clock or a call count, which the runner does not have.
